section1.p: &rfc5888; defines a framework to group SDP 'm' lines for different purposes. A mapping to Jingle as an extension to &xep0166; is defined in this document.
It is anticipated that the primary use of this is with the &bundle; framework used in WebRTC.
The SDP format defined in &rfc5888; is shown below.

This SDP attribute is translated to Jingle as a <group/> element qualified by the 'urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:grouping:0' namespace, as shown below. The semantics is mapped to a 'semantics' attribute. The identification-tags are mapped to content elements whose name attribute is set to the identification-tag.
The <group/> element is included as child of the <jingle/> element.
section1.code: <iq from='romeo@montague.lit/orchard' id='rg6s5134' to='juliet@capulet.lit/balcony' type='set'> <jingle xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:1' action='session-initiate' initiator='romeo@montague.lit/orchard' sid='a73sjjvkla37jfea'> <group xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:grouping:0' semantics='BUNDLE'> <content name='voice'/> <content name='webcam'/> </group> <content creator='initiator' name='voice'> [ ... ] </content> <content creator='initiator' name='webcam'> [ ... ] </content> </jingle> </iq>
section1.p: Note: the identification-tags correspond to the <content/> 'name' attributes. These in turn map to the 'mid' attribute in SDP.

section2.topic: Adding Content to an Existing BUNDLE Group
section2.p: For a group whose 'semantics' attribute is 'BUNDLE', implementations MUST apply the offer/answer procedures defined in &bundle; in addition to the XML mapping defined above.

An initial BUNDLE proposal can contain a single content. If that group is accepted in the initial 'session-initiate'/'session-accept' exchange, a later content addition can extend it as described below. This permits an audio-only session to negotiate its BUNDLE group before video is added. Acceptance of the content alone, without acceptance of the proposed group, does not establish negotiated BUNDLE membership.

Within an active session, the 'content-add'/'content-accept' exchange defined below can extend an already negotiated BUNDLE group. A <group/> element carried by either action MUST describe the complete resulting membership of that group, not only the changed content. Other previously negotiated groups need not be repeated; a group that is not mentioned retains its previously negotiated membership.

If a 'content-add' action does not carry a BUNDLE <group/>, it does not propose a change to previously negotiated BUNDLE membership. A corresponding 'content-accept' without a BUNDLE <group/> likewise leaves the previously negotiated BUNDLE membership unchanged.

A 'content-reject' action rejects the proposed content and leaves previously negotiated BUNDLE membership unchanged. A content removed from the session by 'content-remove' MUST no longer be considered a member of any group that contained it; no separate group update is required merely to reflect removal of content that no longer exists.

Grouping references in these actions are resolved against the current session content definitions together with the new content definitions in the action. A content definition is identified by its 'name' and 'creator' as specified in &xep0166;; repeating that same definition in an answer does not introduce a second content. However, a grouping reference contains only a 'name'. If that name identifies more than one content definition with different creators, the recipient MUST reject the grouping update with a <bad-request/> error rather than guessing which definition is meant.

The IQ result for 'content-add' acknowledges receipt and does not accept the proposed content or its group membership. The proposed membership remains provisional until the corresponding 'content-accept' exchange succeeds. Rejection of the content or an IQ error for the offer leaves previously negotiated membership unchanged. An IQ error in response to a malformed 'content-accept' rejects that answer, not the original 'content-add'; a corrected answer or a 'content-reject' can still resolve the outstanding offer. The receiver of an answer MUST validate that the answer accepts the corresponding proposed content before applying its grouping update. An answer for a different pending content MUST NOT complete this offer.

If a previously negotiated member is removed while an addition is pending, the parties MUST NOT restore that removed content's membership when processing a later answer or IQ result. An implementation can cancel the pending addition using the applicable Jingle content action, or complete it consistently with the remaining session content definitions. Such cancellation does not require termination of the surviving contents.

When a party sends a 'content-add' action that proposes adding the new content to a previously negotiated BUNDLE group, it MUST include the complete proposed BUNDLE <group/>, containing both the previously negotiated members and the new content.

If the recipient accepts that content, its corresponding 'content-accept' action MUST include the complete accepted BUNDLE <group/>. As required by Section 7.5.1 of &bundle;, the recipient MUST NOT accept the newly added content while moving it out of that BUNDLE group in the answer. If the recipient cannot accept the new content as a member of the proposed BUNDLE group, it MUST reject the content using the 'content-reject' action defined by &xep0166;. Omission of the BUNDLE <group/> from such a 'content-accept' MUST NOT be interpreted as accepting the content outside the proposed BUNDLE group.

RFC 9143 permits a bundled media description to be moved out of a previously negotiated BUNDLE group only by a subsequent offer. This specification does not define a Jingle mapping for renegotiating the BUNDLE membership of content that has already been accepted. In particular, the recipient MUST NOT express such a change by omitting the newly added content from the BUNDLE group in the corresponding 'content-accept'.

The following example adds a screen-sharing content to an already negotiated BUNDLE group containing 'voice' and 'webcam'. Although only the new content definition is carried by 'content-add' as required by &xep0166;, the <group/> element contains the complete proposed group membership.

example.caption: Adding a content to an existing BUNDLE group

section2.example: <iq from='romeo@montague.lit/orchard' id='bundle-add-1' to='juliet@capulet.lit/balcony' type='set'> <jingle xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:1' action='content-add' sid='a73sjjvkla37jfea'> <group xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:grouping:0' semantics='BUNDLE'> <content name='voice'/> <content name='webcam'/> <content name='screen'/> </group> <content creator='initiator' name='screen'> [ ... ] </content> </jingle> </iq>
section2.p: If the responder accepts the screen-sharing content, it answers with 'content-accept' and repeats the complete accepted BUNDLE membership.

example.caption: Accepting the content and BUNDLE membership

section2.example: <iq from='juliet@capulet.lit/balcony' id='bundle-accept-1' to='romeo@montague.lit/orchard' type='set'> <jingle xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:1' action='content-accept' sid='a73sjjvkla37jfea'> <group xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:grouping:0' semantics='BUNDLE'> <content name='voice'/> <content name='webcam'/> <content name='screen'/> </group> <content creator='initiator' name='screen'> [ ... ] </content> </jingle> </iq>

section1.p: If an entity supports the grouping framework described in &rfc5888;, it MUST advertise that fact in its responses to &xep0030; information ("disco#info") requests by returning a feature of 'urn:ietf:rfc:5888':
section1.example: <iq type='result' from='herbie@usrobots.lit/home' to='calvin@usrobots.lit/lab' id='disco1'> <query xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#info'> <feature var='urn:xmpp:jingle:1'/> <feature var='urn:ietf:rfc:5888'/> </query> </iq>
section1.p: In order for an application to determine whether an entity supports this protocol, where possible it SHOULD use the dynamic, presence-based profile of service discovery defined in &xep0115;. However, if an application has not received entity capabilities information from an entity, it SHOULD use explicit service discovery instead.
